question: Explain the classical, relative frequency and axiomatic definitions of probability, stating a limitation of the classical definition.
sources: Theory of probability: classical, statistical (relative frequency) and axiomatic approaches (standard principles)

points.label: Classical definition
points.description: If an experiment has n mutually exclusive, exhaustive and equally likely outcomes, of which m are favourable to an event A, then P(A) = m/n.

points.label: Limitation of classical definition
points.description: It cannot be used when outcomes are not equally likely or when the number of outcomes is infinite or unknown.
points.basis: Probability: limitations of the classical definition

points.label: Relative frequency definition
points.description: If an experiment is repeated n times under the same conditions and event A occurs m times, the probability of A is the limit of m/n as n becomes very large.

points.label: Axiomatic definition
points.description: Probability is a function on events of the sample space S such that P(A) ≥ 0 for every event, P(S) = 1, and for mutually exclusive events P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).
